plain.li: I had {NAME} marked on the calendar for weeks. Today I got to watch it kept properly, every bench where it should be.
Organised {NAME} today. Counted the plates twice and still came up one short. Nobody noticed but me.
It's my job to remember what {NAME} means. Today I got to watch everyone else remember it too.
Up before dawn to get {NAME} ready. By supper it looked as if it had arranged itself, which is the idea.
[lowtech] Walked round the whole settlement this morning telling people it was {NAME}. Most of them knew already. I told them anyway.

warm.li: Watching everyone sit down together for {NAME} was worth every hour I spent getting it ready.

cheerful.li: {NAME}! I've been looking forward to it since the last one, and this one was better.

gloomy.li: Kept {NAME} today. Someone always forgets what it's for. I don't.

cold.li: {NAME} was kept as it should be. I saw to it.

plain.li: {PAWN_nameDef} stepped in between {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} before their words got any sharper, and sent them off to different ends of the colony.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} were at it again until {PAWN_nameDef} put a hand on each of their shoulders. It blew over sooner than usual.
{PAWN_nameDef} heard {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} raising their voices and came over with two cups of something hot. The argument didn't outlast the cups.
{PAWN_nameDef} made {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} each say what was really bothering them. It turned out to be smaller than the shouting.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} talked {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} down from a quarrel, gently, without taking either side.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} to stop. They stopped.

cheerful.li: {PAWN_nameDef} broke up a spat between {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} by making them both laugh, which neither of them wanted to do.

gloomy.li: {PAWN_nameDef} got between {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} again. A peacemaker's work is never done, {PAWN_pronoun} says.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} separated {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} and heard each of them out in turn.

plain.li: Enough. Both of you, sit down.
Say it to me first. Then decide if it's worth saying to each other.
This isn't worth a grudge.
Breathe. Then talk.

warm.li: Come on, you two. You're better than this.

cheerful.li: Who wants something hot to drink? Everyone does.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} came by on the morning rounds, looked at the healing and said "better". I'll take it.
{OTHER_nameDef} asked how I was sleeping and wrote the answer down. It's a strange comfort, being written down.
{OTHER_nameDef} made me walk to the door and back while {OTHER_pronoun} watched. Further than yesterday.
{OTHER_nameDef} says another few days of taking it slowly. I asked about work. {OTHER_nameDef} pretended not to hear.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} sat with me a while on the rounds. I think I mend faster when someone is paying attention.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} says I'm the best patient on the rounds! I'm also the only one awake for them.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} keeps telling me I'm getting better. I keep waiting to feel it.

plain.li: Their carts came for everything on the list, and it was all there, counted and stacked. {PLACE} will be ready before the weather turns.
Saw the last of the load onto the carts from {PLACE} today. I knew where every sack was, because I put it there.
The goods went to {PLACE} today, all of them. The fields gave us enough to spare. That's the whole of the job.

warm.li: I hope they sleep easier in {PLACE} tonight. We sent them everything they asked for.

blunt.li: The order for {PLACE}. All of it. Done.

cheerful.li: Every last sack, on time! The drivers from {PLACE} were very impressed with my stacking.

gloomy.li: Sent {PLACE} what they needed. I hope we don't need it ourselves come winter.

cold.li: The order for {PLACE} was filled in full and on time. {FACTION} will remember who filled it.

plain.li: {PAWN_nameDef}, who keeps the colony's animals, helped {OTHER_nameDef} bury {PET_nameDef}, and had a story about the animal that {OTHER_nameDef} had never heard.
{PAWN_nameDef} sat with {OTHER_nameDef} by the pens that evening. Neither of them said much. {PET_nameDef}'s place in the straw was still warm.
{PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef} that {PET_nameDef} had as good a life as any animal could have here, and meant it.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} came to find {OTHER_nameDef} as soon as {PAWN_pronoun} heard about {PET_nameDef}, and stayed until it was dark.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} dug the grave for {PET_nameDef} with {OTHER_nameDef}. Didn't need to be asked.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef} plainly that nothing could have been done for {PET_nameDef}. It seemed to help.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} came home to find {PET_nameDef} fed, brushed and fatter than before. {PAWN_nameDef} had been looking after it.
{PAWN_nameDef} kept an eye on {PET_nameDef} while {OTHER_nameDef} was away, and handed it back with a list of everything it had got up to.
{PET_nameDef} ran to meet {OTHER_nameDef} at the edge of the colony. {PAWN_nameDef} says it waited by the door every evening.

cheerful.li: {PAWN_nameDef} says {PET_nameDef} behaved perfectly while {OTHER_nameDef} was away. {PET_nameDef} looks as if that isn't the whole story.

plain.li: When the fighting was over, {PAWN_nameDef} walked the line and had a word with everyone who had stood in it.
{PAWN_nameDef} went round the defenders after the fight, a hand on each shoulder, asking who needed what.
The marshal, {PAWN_nameDef}, sat with the fighters after the battle until the shaking stopped, {PAWN_possessive} own included.
[lowtech] After the fight {PAWN_nameDef} passed a waterskin down the line and named each of them, one by one, for what they had done.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} checked on every fighter after the battle. Short words. They helped.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} went over the fight with each of those who stood in it: what went well, what to do next time.

plain.li: They kept {NAME} today. I couldn't face it. I sat on my bed and listened to them through the wall.
Everyone went to {NAME}. Nobody made me go, and I was grateful for that.
I'm not ready for feasts. Maybe next year.
Someone brought me a plate from {NAME} and left it by the door without a word.

warm.li: I told them to go and enjoy {NAME} without me. They should. I'll come next time.

cheerful.li: Even I didn't feel like a party today. That's how I know how bad it is.

gloomy.li: They were singing for {NAME}. I don't know how anyone sings.

cold.li: I did not go to {NAME}. It would have been a performance, and I had none in me.

plain.li: {PET_nameDef} wouldn't leave {PAWN_nameDef}'s side all afternoon, and {PAWN_nameDef} didn't want it to.
{PAWN_nameDef} spent an hour with {PET_nameDef}, saying nothing at all, and came back a little steadier.
{PET_nameDef} found {PAWN_nameDef} sitting alone and lay down across {PAWN_possessive} feet.
Grief is quieter with an animal leaning against you, {PAWN_nameDef} says. {PET_nameDef} has been doing a lot of leaning.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} has been spending time with {PET_nameDef}, who asks no questions, which is the point.

plain.li: Still not strong, but they found me a seat near the middle and I stayed to the end. Better medicine than the bed.
First gathering since I took ill. I sat the whole time and nobody minded.
They brought the food to me so I didn't have to stand. I laughed more than I have in weeks.

warm.li: Everyone came over to my chair at some point. I felt like the guest of honour, which I suppose I was.

blunt.li: Went to the gathering. Sat. Good.

cheerful.li: I wasn't going to miss that! Even if I did have to be helped to my seat.

gloomy.li: Went, sat in a corner, watched everyone else enjoy themselves. Still, better than the ceiling.

cold.li: I attended the gathering from a chair. The company did more good than the rest would have.

plain.li: [day] {NAME} helped more than I expected. For an evening the rest of it went quiet.
[day] We kept {NAME} together, and somewhere in the middle of it I stopped feeling so far from everyone.
[day] I almost didn't go to {NAME}. I'm glad I did.
[favour] {FACTION} came back to repay what we once did for them. Kindness comes round after all. I needed to see that.
[favour] An envoy from {FACTION}, to settle an old debt. It made me think the world isn't as cold as I'd decided.
[camp] {NAME} has gone on with the camp. We talked most nights by their fire. I feel more like myself for it.
[camp] I'll miss {NAME}. Strange, how a stranger can say exactly what you needed to hear.
[recovered] Back on my feet properly today. Lying in bed I had a lot of time to think. Now I can do something about it.
[recovered] Strong again. Being laid up made a few things clearer.

warm.li: [day] Everyone together for {NAME}. I needed that more than I knew.
[recovered] Everyone was so kind while I was ill. I mean to pay it back, starting now.
[camp] I hope {NAME}'s road is a kind one. {NAME} was kind to me.

blunt.li: [favour] {FACTION} paid back what they owed. Good.

cheerful.li: [day] What a day! {NAME} always lifts me.
[recovered] Up and about! Watch out, everyone.

gloomy.li: [day] {NAME} was a kind of relief. They don't come often.
[recovered] Well again. I suppose that's something.

cold.li: [favour] {FACTION} honoured their debt. That is worth noting.
[camp] {NAME} was good company. The conversations were useful.

plain.li: Some of us have more to answer for than others. Isn't that right, {OTHER_nameDef}?
I'd trust that idea more if everyone at this table were honest about where they come from.
{OTHER_nameDef} knows exactly what I mean.
Funny who talks loudest about trust.

warm.li: I won't say it here, {OTHER_nameDef}. But you should.

cheerful.li: Shall we all say one true thing about ourselves? {OTHER_nameDef} can go first.

gloomy.li: Everyone here has something they aren't saying. Some more than others.

cold.li: Before we vote, perhaps {OTHER_nameDef} has something to tell the council.
